title: A clinical trial to learn more about the effects of GIA632 in people with lichen planus
official: A Phase IIb multicenter, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, dose-range study to assess the efficacy and safety of GIA632 in participants with moderate to severe cutaneous lichen planus, followed by an extension period
summary: Main objective: To establish and characterize the dose-response relationship of respective intervention and estimate the treatment effect of the targeted doses versus placebo with respect to Investigator’s Global Assessment response at Week 16 in participants with cLP inadequately controlled by topical treatment or for whom such treatment is not advisable.
criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
1. Male or female (as assigned at birth) participants ≥ 18 years of age at the time of screening.
2. Individuals with a diagnosis of cLP, confirmed •	histologically by a skin biopsy (either historically within 1 year prior to screening or at screening if historical one not available), and  •	by physical examination by the investigator at screening.
3. Moderate to severe cLP, as defined by: •	IGA (Investigator’s Global Assessment) ≥ 3 at Screening and Baseline •	Peak 24 hours PP-NRS ≥ 4 (weekly mean of daily score from eDiary during last 7 days of screening period), assessed at Baseline.
4. Two or more body regions affected (any two or more of the following: head and neck, trunk, upper extremities including hands, lower extremities including feet) or 3% or more of total body surface area (BSA) are affected, assessed at Baseline.
5. Diagnosis of cLP inadequately controlled by at least one topical treatment for at least 3 months (either via continuous use or burst and taper regimen), or such treatment being considered not advisable, as per investigator judgement, assessed at screening. Topical treatment includes, but is not limited to, topical corticosteroids, topical calcineurin inhibitors, topical cholecalciferol analogues, topical PDE4 inhibitors, topical JAK inhibitors, and topical aryl hydrocarbon receptor agonists.
Exclusion criteria:
1. Individuals unable or unwilling to follow the study procedures, handle the electronic diary (eDiary), and/or to complete the study-related questionnaires.
2. Diagnosis of drug-induced lichen planus (lichenoid drug eruption) or lichen planus pigmentosus.
3. Diagnosis of predominantly hypertrophic or predominantly bullous variant of cLP, as determined by the investigator at screening and baseline. Note: Some hypertrophic or bullous lesions may be present and still allow participant inclusion, provided that papular/plaque type morphology remains the predominant LP presentation, per investigator judgment.
4. Presence of skin conditions that may interfere with study assessments, including histologic findings in the biopsy, as assessed at screening and baseline.
5. Previous exposure to biologic drugs directly targeting IL-15 or any subunit of the IL-15 receptor.
6. Plans for administration of live vaccines during the study period or within 4 weeks before randomization, or within 16 weeks after study completion.
7. Use of prohibited medication and treatments.
